About Vercel:

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.

About The Role

The next generation of software won’t just be used by people — it’ll be built and shipped by agents. Builds are where that happens, and they’re the beating heart of Vercel. Whether an idea starts in v0, in an agent, or in an engineer’s editor, every customer builds — and millions of builds flow through our systems every day.

As an engineer on the Agentic Infrastructure team, you’ll take ownership of the systems that carry that work at scale. You won’t just contribute features — you’ll be responsible for the design, reliability, and evolution of the platform itself. You’ll make decisions that shape performance, define best practices, and ensure the workflows that Vercel, our customers, and their agents depend on are fast, resilient, and secure.

This role blends product thinking with deep systems ownership. You’ll partner with teams across Vercel to build and operate the agentic infrastructure that determines how software actually ships.

We’re looking for engineers who want to own high-scale systems end-to-end, thrive on improving the developer/agent experience, and are driven to have a lasting impact on how modern software gets built and delivered.

What you’ll do

Own and evolve the infrastructure that powers Vercel’s build and deployment lifecycle — from handling webhooks to designing resilient database schemas and building scalable APIs.
Design and operate high-performance microservices that process millions of builds daily, ensuring speed, reliability, and developer delight.
Lead projects end-to-end: from identifying opportunities to defining technical direction and delivering improvements in performance, reliability, and developer experience.
Collaborate across teams to align infrastructure with company-wide goals and ensure seamless developer workflows.
Shape the long-term vision of agentic infrastructure at Vercel by setting standards for scalability, reliability, and developer productivity.
Participate in the on-call rotation, taking responsibility for the reliability of critical systems.
Contribute to the open-source community, representing Vercel’s commitment to advancing developer tools globally.
Write clean, efficient, tested, and well-documented code that others can build upon confidently.

What you need

3+ years of experience designing, building, and operating backend applications and distributed systems at scale.
Strong proficiency in JavaScript/TypeScript, with the ability to navigate and improve complex systems.
Strong proficiency with cloud infrastructure (AWS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform)
A track record of end-to-end ownership — from design and implementation through to long-term operation in production.
Skilled at cross-team collaboration, able to influence priorities and drive alignment toward shared goals.
Able to reason about technical direction and architectural tradeoffs, balancing long-term vision with pragmatic delivery.
Invested in the people around you — through mentorship, code review, or simply raising the bar on how the team builds.
Curious, eager to learn, and motivated to push the boundaries of how modern software gets built and shipped.

Bonus if you

Are familiar with React or Next.js
Have experience with DynamoDB
Have worked to develop a CI/CD platform or internal developer platform used by other engineers or by agents.
Have experience contributing to or participating in open-source projects.
Have experience optimizing build systems for monorepos or polyrepo setups.
Have experience with build caching, artifact storage, or dependency management at scale.

Benefits & Compensation:

Competitive compensation package, including equity.
Inclusive Healthcare Package.
Learn and Grow - we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills.
Flexible Time Off.
We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed.

The base pay range for this role is $196,000.00 - $294,000.00. Actual salary will be based on job-related skills, experience, and location. Compensation outside of San Francisco may be adjusted based on employee location. The total compensation package may include benefits, equity-based compensation, and eligibility for a company bonus or variable pay program depending on the role. Your recruiter can share more details during the hiring process.

jobs.description:
Senior Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Applications

Enterprise Platform Group

Commercialization (Quote-to-Cash)
Mountain View, CA

As a Senior Staff Software Engineer on the Agentic Applications team, you will be the hands-on technical lead for how Databricks quotes, orders, bills and recognizes revenue. Your core function is to build bespoke first-party, agents-first applications built on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. You will own the technical architecture end to end, from quote to cash. You will design agents that work reliably inside revenue-critical workflows, set the engineering standards the team builds on, and make sure every agent-assisted decision can be observed, audited and trusted by Finance, Deal Desk and Sales.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role, not a people-management role. You will write code, review designs, and be the most senior technical voice in a domain that touches every dollar Databricks books.

The impact you'll have

Own the agentic architecture for Quote-to-Cash. Define and lead the target technical architecture across Configure-Price-Quote, deal management, ordering, subscriptions, investments, billing and revenue recognition. Drive the move from vendor-configured workflows to first-party, AI-native applications built on Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Unity Catalog and Mosaic AI.
Build production agents that sellers and Deal Desk trust. Design and ship LLM-powered agents for deal guidance, quote generation and summarization, multi-option proposals, approval insights, and pricing and discount recommendations. Work directly with sales, Deal Desk and Finance to define what "good" looks like for each workflow.
Make agent reliability a core system property. Own the eval and quality system for this domain: per-workflow quality criteria, offline eval suites, LLM-as-judge and human-labeled benchmarks, behavioral regression testing in CI/CD, online tracing, and feedback loops that improve agents based on what users approve, edit and reject.
Design human-in-the-loop controls for revenue-critical decisions. Build the separation between what an agent proposes and what gets committed, plus diff-based review, approval routing, audit logging, and policy guardrails. Together these decide when an agent can act on its own and when a person has to approve, especially for pricing, discounting, contract terms and order creation.
Treat systems of record as agent tools. Architect tool-calling and MCP-style interfaces that give agents governed, run-time access to pricing, product catalog, order, contract, subscription and billing data. Follow single-source-of-truth principles across CRM, ERP and billing systems.
Protect financial integrity at scale. Make sure agent-assisted quoting and ordering produce accurate, compliance-grade outputs downstream: order validation, billing, invoicing and revenue recognition, where errors directly affect financial reporting.
Lead the migration path. Act as the bridge between today's production quoting platform and the target agentic architecture. Sequence the migration so the business keeps scaling without disruption, and decide what to retire, rebuild or wrap.
Raise the engineering bar. Lead architecture reviews, establish design patterns for agents (orchestration, memory, retrieval, tool use, multi-agent coordination), and mentor senior and mid-level engineers on production-grade agentic engineering.
Earn cross-functional credibility. Partner with Finance, Deal Desk, Sales Ops, Legal and the broader Platform engineering org. Turn complex commercial processes into clear technical roadmaps and measurable business outcomes.

What We Look For

12+ years of software engineering experience, with a clear track record of technical leadership and ownership of large-scale production systems.
3+ years of hands-on experience building and running LLM-powered or agentic applications in production, such as agents, RAG pipelines, tool use, multi-agent orchestration (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, DSPy or equivalent), and evaluation frameworks for generative outputs.
Strong backend and distributed-systems skills: API and service design, data modeling, idempotency, consistency and transactional integrity, and observability.
Proven experience designing human-in-the-loop systems: approval workflows, review interfaces, audit trails, and guardrails for probabilistic systems operating in regulated or high-stakes domains.
Experience leading technical architecture for complex business domains, ideally Quote-to-Cash, Order-to-Revenue, billing, pricing or other revenue-critical enterprise systems.
Full-stack fluency. You are comfortable across modern web frameworks (React/TypeScript), backend services (Python, Java, Scala or Go), and data platforms.
Ability to work directly with non-engineering stakeholders and turn ambiguous business workflows into clear agent and system architecture.
Experience mentoring engineers and improving technical execution across a team, without relying on positional authority.

Nice to have

Domain experience with CPQ, deal management, subscription management, or revenue recognition in a high-growth SaaS or consumption-based business.
Experience building first-party applications on top of, or as replacements for, enterprise SaaS platforms (e.g., Salesforce CPQ/Revenue Cloud, NetSuite, Zuora). Platform-specific configuration expertise is a plus but not a requirement.
Experience with the Databricks platform (Databricks Apps, Lakebase, Unity Catalog, Mosaic AI Agent Framework, MLflow tracing and evaluation).

jobs.description:
About Scribe

Scribe is where exceptional people come to do the best work of their careers. More than 94% of the Fortune 500 use Scribe to own their specialized intelligence: the unique way their teams work, decide, and get things done. Our Specialized Intelligence platform automatically captures how work happens and turns it into a living asset for people and AI agents.

We're growing fast. Since our founding in 2019, we've reached 7 million users across 600,000 businesses. Based in San Francisco, we're a LinkedIn Top Startup, valued at over $1B, and backed by leading investors. Join us in our mission to transform how people work.

tl;dr – Why this role matters

At Scribe, data is the foundation of how we make decisions — we take it very seriously
. With 5M+ users and a fast-growing self-serve business, our product team ships quickly and needs to know what’s working, for whom, and why. We’re looking for our first product data scientist to answer our most important questions about how customers use Scribe, bring rigor to how we experiment, and lay the foundation of product data science that will shape the next generation of product investments.

Hiring Manage
r: Melanie Herscher, Head of Data

About The Role

As the first Senior Data Scientist for Product, you’ll partner with our product, design, and engineering teams to understand user behavior, identify opportunities, and measure the impact of what we build. Reporting directly to the Head of Data, you’ll define how Scribe approaches product analytics and experimentation, and set the standards that future data scientists will build on. From day one, you’ll also have the opportunity to mentor members of the data team and raise the bar for analytical rigor across Scribe.

This role is highly visible, working directly with executive leadership as well as the product managers and engineers who own each area of the product. You will transform raw data from Scribe’s 5M+ users into clear, actionable insights, and your work will be central to how we grow our self-serve business and decide where to invest next.

Key Responsibilities Of This Role Include

Partner with product teams to drive insights, identifying opportunities and understanding user behavior, engagement, retention, and long-term trends across the Scribe product.
Own experimentation at Scribe by designing and analyzing experiments, and developing and socializing a rigorous culture of experimentation throughout the company.
Lead with hypotheses, developing and testing them with data rather than only looking for patterns in the data already in front of us.
Define and monitor key product metrics through consistent tracking, KPIs, and dashboards, and produce new datasets that unlock business opportunities.
Play a foundational role in building product data culture at Scribe through reproducible work, improved processes, and better tooling.
Help shape the team as it grows, with the opportunity to mentor teammates on statistics, experimentation, and analytical best practices.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You’d be a great fit for this role if this sounds like you:

Have 8+ years of experience as a data scientist or data analyst with significant time partnering with product teams on products that customers love
Strong knowledge of statistics and experimental design, with hands-on experience running A/B tests and making sound calls when experiments aren’t possible
Strong technical proficiency in our tech stack – Snowflake, Sigma, Mixpanel, dbt cloud, and Looker – with expert SQL and fluency in Python or R
Customer mindset, adept at balancing quantitative data with qualitative insights to drive product decisions, and an excellent storyteller in writing and visualizations
Low ego. You care about building things and recognize that this may require rolling your sleeves up, getting in the trenches, and owning everything from instrumentation to analysis
Proactive, high-output orientation. You push insights and data onto teams rather than waiting for requests to emerge from them
Outcomes over output. You thrive on creating business value and know when to run a rigorous experiment v/s doing ugly napkin math to bias towards action
Experience building technical and semantic infrastructure to power internal natural language agents and agentic automation

Bonus Points

Experience working in high-paced Enterprise SaaS startups, with a strong self-serve motion
Experience as the first or founding data scientist on a product team
Experience creating a step-function change in a product team’s decision-making with the help of AI tooling
Experience deploying machine learning models in Production
Experience mentoring analysts or data scientists

Benefits

Healthcare Coverage – Comprehensive health, dental, and vision plans, including two $0/month medical plan options for employees
Equity – Ownership in what we're building
401(k) Plan – through Vestwell
Flex Benefit – $500/year for home office equipment, productivity tools, learning & development or fitness/wellness
Commuter Benefits – $100/month for SF based employees
PTO – Flexible paid time off and company holidays
Parental Leave – Paid leave to support growing families
Wellness & Family Support – Free Talkspace membership, One Medical access (location-dependent), and Kindbody discounts for family planning

At Scribe, we celebrate our differences and are committed to creating a workplace where all employees feel supported and empowered to do their best work. Scribe is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Millions of people around the world come to our platform to find creative ideas, dream about new possibilities and plan for memories that will last a lifetime. At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.

Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.

At Pinterest, AI isn't just a feature, it's a powerful partner that augments our creativity and amplifies our impact, and we’re looking for candidates who are excited to be a part of that. To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.

Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here.

Our Retrieval team builds shared machine learning capabilities that help Pinterest connect people with relevant ideas. We are looking for a Staff Machine Learning Engineer to advance how we develop those capabilities through agentic AI.

You will work closely with other technical leaders while remaining hands-on with the hardest engineering and modeling problems.

You will also contribute to generative retrieval, with a particular focus on Semantic IDs: learning structured representations of content that recommendation models can generate and use to retrieve relevant items. This role combines applied AI research, production engineering and technical leadership, with opportunities to improve both our recommendation models and the way engineers build them.

Build LLM agents that connect hypothesis generation, implementation, experiment execution, evaluation and learning from previous results.

An early-stage, venture-backed AI startup automating the work of corporate finance teams.

There's no management layer between you and the CTO, and you'll spend real time with customers and controllers learning how their finance workflows actually run.

The team is hiring 2 platform engineers at once, so you'll be shaping the foundation alongside another senior builder rather than alone. What you'll do

Build and own the core agent platform: frameworks, orchestration, verification, observability, and the tooling other engineering pods ship on
Design the data platform that ingests, normalizes, and reconciles records from ERPs, banks, billing, payroll, and CRM systems
Sit with finance teams and controllers to understand their workflows, then turn what you learn into reusable platform building blocks
Make architecture calls when the path isn't clear, find the bottlenecks, and ship full-stack when a problem needs it
Lead cross-team technical work that lets the whole engineering org move faster as revenue grows

What you must bring

4+ years of backend or platform software engineering, primarily in Python
A track record of building foundational platform or infrastructure systems that run at scale

jobs.description:
Small businesses represent 99.9% of all companies, yet they're still forced to choose between clunky, outdated enterprise phone systems or their personal phones. This multi-billion dollar market has been overlooked for decades, left to cobble together solutions that slow them down instead of helping them grow.

Quo is changing that. We bring calls, texts, and customer information together into one easy-to-use, AI-powered platform. We're not just building a phone system. We're setting a new standard for how businesses connect with their customers.

Driven by our values, we move fast, build with determination, and obsess over delivering value to the businesses that have been underserved for far too long.

Today, Quo is trusted by more than 120,000 companies and rated #1 in customer satisfaction on G2. We're backed by Y Combinator, Tiger Global, Craft Ventures, Slow Ventures, and other top-tier investors. It's safe to say we're onto something big.

About The Role

Our AI Agent Platform team owns the platform behind nearly all of Quo's customer-facing AI agents. That includes Sona, our AI agent for calls and texts, and Quo Agent, the workspace agent we've just launched. Agents are already live with customers, so this isn't basic plumbing. The hard problems are the ones ahead.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll be the hands-on technical lead for the team. You'll set the technical direction for how agents are built and run at Quo, and you'll write a lot of the code that gets us there. Your work will shape how every customer experiences AI inside Quo, and how every other team at Quo builds with it.

We're bringing AI work that grew up in separate teams onto one shared platform. This role is central to that, and you'll have real ownership from day one.

Some Of The Things You’ll Do

Own the architecture of the agent platform: how any team at Quo creates and runs an agent, the shared pool of tools and integrations agents call, the single layer every model call goes through, and the execution engine that turns model output into real API and tool calls.
Build advanced orchestration, from one agent coordinating five or more subagents to long-running agents that work on a task for hours.
Design memory and self-learning, so our agents get better from customer feedback over time.
Drive the scale, performance, reliability and cost of agent execution as usage grows across calls, texts and the workspace.
Make it easy for other teams to build on the platform. You'll be its best advocate, with clear docs, good defaults and a lot of pairing.
Mentor engineers through design reviews, code reviews and hands-on coaching, raising the bar for the whole AI domain.
Stay close to what's happening in LLMs and agent tooling, and turn what you learn into practical roadmap proposals.

Tech Stack & Tools

Node and TypeScript on the backend
Event-driven microservices with Temporal and RabbitMQ at the centre
Kubernetes on AWS
Postgres, MongoDB, Elasticsearch and Redis
Datadog for observability
Web (React), iOS and Android clients on the other side of the API

Language is not a filter. If you've built the right things in Go, Python, Java or anything else, we'd rather talk to you than to someone who knows Node but hasn't.

About You

You've built and scaled the backend of a product with a lot of real users, and you've led the architecture of business-critical services.
You've shipped LLM-powered systems to production, ideally an agent platform or orchestration layer. If you haven't built an agent platform yet but have built something close, like an ML platform, a workflow engine or real-time communications infrastructure, and you've gone deep on LLMs hands-on, we'd still love to talk.
You're strong in TypeScript and Node, or you're fluent in another backend language and keen to ramp up on ours.
You have high agency. You see what needs doing, pick it up and move it forward without waiting to be asked.
You learn fast and you're plugged into the AI world. You know what's changing in models, agent frameworks and tooling, and you have opinions about it.
You write clear design docs, explain trade-offs well and bring other engineers and teams along with you.
You care about customers. You weigh technical decisions against the experience of a small business owner using our product every day.

Bonus Points If You

Have run Temporal or another durable workflow engine in production.
Have worked on customer-facing AI products, not only internal developer tooling.
Have founded or been early at a startup.

Compensation

The annual base salary range for this position is as follows, plus equity and benefits:

SF Bay Area, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Boston, New York, and Washington, DC Metro: $205,000 - $242,000 USD
All other US Locations: $186,000 - $217,000 USD
Canada: $189,000 - $222,000 CAD

Salary is just one component of Quo’s total compensation package. Your total rewards package will include equity, extensive medical coverage, a monthly lifestyle stipend, and a flexible PTO policy.

Who we are

We're a remote-first company with a culture of trust, autonomy, and action. As we rapidly grow, we're intentionally building communities in a handful of hub cities while continuing to hire great talent wherever they happen to live. If you're looking for a place to do your best work, we'd love to hear from you.

And remember, there's no such thing as a 'perfect' candidate. We're looking for optimists with grit and determination, who are excited to face the challenges of a growing startup. Quo is the type of company where you can grow, and we encourage you to apply for this role even if you don't think you meet all the requirements.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse work environment. It is important that you are able to bring your authentic self to work every day. About Hilbert

Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes.

From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We’re also co-building alongside leading AI companies.

Position Overview

Hilbert is building a reasoning engine that must navigate non-deterministic user behavior across data silos. Our demand intelligence platform doesn’t just call APIs. It solves the hard problem of orchestrating multi-step inference over messy, high-stakes enterprise data where deterministic answers don’t exist.

We’re looking for an AI Engineer who can build production-grade AI systems end-to-end, from prototype to pipeline to product, with the ownership and urgency of a startup culture.

This is not a “wire up a prompt chain and move on” role. You’ll own core pieces of the AI stack that power Hilbert’s platform: designing agent architectures, building evaluation systems, and making hard tradeoffs between accuracy, latency, and cost in production. You’ll ship fast while the spec is still evolving, and you’ll explain what you’re building (and why) clearly to the rest of the team. If you think in systems, have opinions about how agentic workflows should actually work, and want to build AI products that drive real enterprise outcomes, we want to meet you.

What you’ll own first: evaluation and testing for our agents

Hilbert’s agents are in production with enterprise customers today. Before we expand what they do, we need to know, reproducibly, when a change makes them better or worse. You’ll design the eval harness, define what “correct” means for a multi-step agent trajectory, build the regression gates that run before anything ships, and turn production failures into test cases. From there, your scope widens to retrieval, orchestration, and execution across the AI stack.

What You’ll Do

Own the evaluation layer for our agents: harnesses, metrics, golden datasets, regression gates, and human-in-the-loop review.
Architect and implement agent workflows using LangChain, LangGraph, or equivalent, including state memory, routing, tool registries, and recovery paths.
Own systems from experimentation through production, and operate them once they’re live: tracing, monitoring, latency, cost-per-task budgeting, and on-call for what you build.
Diagnose real production failures (hallucination, tool misuse, retrieval misses, silent degradation) and turn each one into a durable fix and a test.
Set the technical standard for agent work at Hilbert: review designs, define patterns others build on, and raise the bar across the team.
Collaborate closely with the founding team and cross-functional partners, communicating tradeoffs, progress, and technical decisions clearly.
Make pragmatic engineering decisions under ambiguity: ship, learn, iterate.

Our current hurdles: the kinds of problems you’ll walk into on day one

Intelligent retrieval across different approaches. Our agents need the right information at exactly the right moment. The challenge isn’t picking one retrieval method. It’s combining RAG, graph-based retrieval, and other approaches into one strategy that fetches the most relevant content exactly when the agent needs it, no more and no less.
Agentic workflows that solve real-world problems. Workflows have to be robust enough to handle the unexpected. When an agent hits an edge case, missing data, or a situation it wasn’t designed for, it needs to reason through it: use the context it has, escalate to a human when it can’t, and never fail silently.
Evaluation beyond vibes. We need systematic, reproducible evals that actually predict real-world performance. If you’ve built custom evaluators for RAG or agent workflows, we want to talk.
Execution and real-world integration. An agent that only surfaces insights isn’t enough. We’re building systems where agents take action: integrating with external platforms, executing workflows, and doing real work with the information they have, with human-in-the-loop checkpoints that keep enterprise trust intact.

Who Thrives In The Role

We care about what you’ve shipped and how you think. We expect 4+ years of building production software, with at least 2 of those on LLM or agentic systems that real users depend on.

Must-haves

4+ years of production software engineering (APIs, services, data infrastructure). You’ve owned code other people depended on, with tests, CI/CD, and on-call attached.
2+ years building LLM or agent systems that shipped to production and were adopted by real users. Not internal demos, not prototypes. Be ready to talk about what broke in production and what you did about it.
Hands-on experience with LangChain, LangGraph, or equivalent agent/orchestration frameworks. You’ve built with them, hit their limits, and worked around them. You go well beyond following tutorials.
Clear, confident communication. You can explain a technical decision to a non-technical founder and debate architecture tradeoffs with a senior engineer. Communication isn’t a nice-to-have here; it’s core to the role.
Ownership. You don’t wait for tickets. You see what needs to be built, raise your hand, and ship it.
Comfort with ambiguity. AI products evolve fast and requirements change. You’re energized by figuring it out.
Startup speed. You move without waiting for permission, and you know which decisions deserve a day of thought and which deserve an hour.

Strong Pluses

Deep experience with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): hybrid and graph retrieval, chunking and embedding strategy, ranking, grounding.
Observability for LLM systems (Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, or equivalent) and cost/latency optimization.
MCP, tool-calling frameworks, structured output, and constrained decoding.
Experience at early-stage startups or high-growth environments where you wore multiple hats.

You might be:

A backend engineer who went deep on LLMs and never looked back. An ML engineer who realized they love building products, not just models. A startup CTO who wants to go deep on AI at a company where the stack is the product. Someone who’s been hacking on agents and pipelines on nights and weekends and wants to do it full-time with real enterprise stakes. What matters: you ship, you own it, and you communicate like a teammate, not a silo.

jobs.description:
About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Ramp Labs

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both.

About The Role

Every model decision at Ramp Labs runs through a benchmark. Which model to route to. Whether a post-training run worked. Whether an agent is ready to post a corrective journal entry to a customer's ledger without a human in the loop.

You'll own Ramp's benchmarking effort. You'll turn real finance work (expense policy review, invoice coding, month-end close, spreadsheet Q&A) into benchmarks and RL environments, build the graders, and tell the team what is actually improving.

What You’ll Do

Build benchmarks from real workflows: turn agent traces, customer edge cases and expert labels into versioned benchmark suites for long-horizon agents that run for hours across tools and systems, plus tool use, multi-step reasoning and financial judgment
Own the benchmarking effort: decide what we measure, run benchmark suites across models and agent versions, and report results the team makes decisions on
Design graders: rubrics, programmatic checks and llm-as-judge, calibrated against human agreement, with a clear view of where each one breaks
Close the loop with post-training: turn evals into reward functions and RL environments, and catch reward hacking and contamination before they ship
Publish external benchmarks and write-ups on how models perform at real finance work

What You Need

Hands-on experience building LLM benchmarks or evals that people used to make real decisions
Strong Python and software engineering; your eval code is reproducible and fast
Statistical judgment: variance, confidence intervals, sample size, inter-rater agreement, and knowing when a delta is noise
Working knowledge of post-training (SFT, RL with verifiable rewards) and how evals feed into it
Comfort with SQL and large datasets; you'll work directly from production traces
Taste for what is worth measuring

Nice-to-Have

Industry experience on an eval, benchmarking or post-training team
Built RL environments or verifiers for agentic tasks
Published benchmark or evaluation research (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICML, ACL)
Built or contributed to eval frameworks (verifiers, lm-evaluation-harness, HELM or similar)
Familiarity with accounting, finance or other expert-domain work
Public work we can look at: a benchmark, an eval suite, a failure-analysis write-up

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About Ramp Labs

Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 70,000+ companies use to move money. We think the defensible part of an AI product is the loop: proprietary environments, evals that track what customers care about, and models trained against both.

About The Role

Every model decision at Ramp Labs runs through a benchmark. Which model to route to. Whether a post-training run worked. Whether an agent is ready to post a corrective journal entry to a customer's ledger without a human in the loop.

You'll own Ramp's benchmarking effort. You'll turn real finance work (expense policy review, invoice coding, month-end close, spreadsheet Q&A) into benchmarks and RL environments, build the graders, and tell the team what is actually improving.

What You’ll Do

Build benchmarks from real workflows: turn agent traces, customer edge cases and expert labels into versioned benchmark suites for long-horizon agents that run for hours across tools and systems, plus tool use, multi-step reasoning and financial judgment
Own the benchmarking effort: decide what we measure, run benchmark suites across models and agent versions, and report results the team makes decisions on
Design graders: rubrics, programmatic checks and llm-as-judge, calibrated against human agreement, with a clear view of where each one breaks
Close the loop with post-training: turn evals into reward functions and RL environments, and catch reward hacking and contamination before they ship
Publish external benchmarks and write-ups on how models perform at real finance work

What You Need

Hands-on experience building LLM benchmarks or evals that people used to make real decisions
Strong Python and software engineering; your eval code is reproducible and fast
Statistical judgment: variance, confidence intervals, sample size, inter-rater agreement, and knowing when a delta is noise
Working knowledge of post-training (SFT, RL with verifiable rewards) and how evals feed into it
Comfort with SQL and large datasets; you'll work directly from production traces
Taste for what is worth measuring

Nice-to-Have

Industry experience on an eval, benchmarking or post-training team
Built RL environments or verifiers for agentic tasks
Published benchmark or evaluation research (NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks, ICML, ACL)
Built or contributed to eval frameworks (verifiers, lm-evaluation-harness, HELM or similar)
Familiarity with accounting, finance or other expert-domain work
Public work we can look at: a benchmark, an eval suite, a failure-analysis write-up
